glance.what: Disaster relief aid on Solana: funds arrive fast, spendable only at verified local stores.
glance.why: Gets money to people fast after storms, with price gouging blocked.

record.what_it_is: A simulated disaster-relief system on Solana: a multi-hazard model scores census tracts at hurricane landfall, relief tokens are airdropped to household wallets, spendable only at registered local stores under on-chain rules, with a Grok shopping agent and an anomaly oracle that suspends price gougers.
record.problem_and_user: Hurricane survivors who wait weeks for restricted aid or receive fast but misusable cash; implied users are residents, merchants and disaster officials.
record.one_line_pitch: Disaster relief market on Solana where a storm-impact model triggers instant aid airdrops to affected households redeemable at local stores.
record.problem_statement: Disaster food aid after Hurricane Helene took nearly a month to open and required in-person applications.
record.devpost_tagline: EBT for disasters, on Solana. Aid lands 0.93s after the storm hits, spendable only at verified local stores. Grok does the shopping, an ML oracle shuts down price gougers on chain.
devpost_first_sections: Hurricane Helene hit Georgia on September 26, 2024. Georgia's disaster food stamps didn't open until October 21, almost a month later. You had to apply in person with an ID, and some counties waited about seven weeks. FEMA's emergency payment was around $750, and that came later too. The slow part isn't sending money. It's figuring out who needs it, and making sure it actually gets spent on water, food and medicine instead of getting resold or eaten up by price gouging. After Katrina, the GAO estimated $600M to $1.4B in improper or fraudulent FEMA aid. After Helene, Georgia's Attorney General got around 400 price gouging complaints. Rescu is a disaster relief market built on Solana. Aid airdropped in seconds. Figures out who needs help. A model looks at the storm itself (wind, rain flooding, storm surge, mobile homes and how vulnerable each neighborhood is) and decides who gets how much, right at landfall. No paperwork, no waiting. Airdrops the aid. An official clicks Declare disaster & fund , and "Relief Dollars" go out on Solana as the storm moves. Each neighborhood gets paid the moment the winds reach it. The median time from the storm hitting a home to money in the wallet was 0.93 seconds . Puts the rules inside the money. Every payment is checked on-chain: registered stores only, inside the disaster zone, max $200

glance.what: A cute LED Pomodoro study timer to break unproductive slumps.
glance.for_whom: Students stuck in unproductive study ruts
glance.why: Helps you focus and get working with timed Pomodoro sessions.

record.what_it_is: An Arduino hardware Pomodoro timer built from 48 LEDs on six branches that show study and break progress by turning rows off over time and flashing indicator lights at phase ends.
record.problem_and_user: A student (the builder) who uses 50 minutes study and 5 minutes break and wants a cute visual timer to keep on task.
record.one_line_pitch: Solo Arduino Pomodoro timer using rows of LEDs that turn off every ten minutes to show remaining study time.
record.problem_statement: Study sessions using the Pomodoro method lack a simple visible cue of how much time remains.
record.devpost_tagline: Are you stuck in a unproductive rut? Do you need something cute and functional to get you working? Fear not! Using the Pomodoro technique, the Bye Bye Study Blues LED timer is the perfect thing.
devpost_first_sections: I'm a computer engineering major, and I knew I'd want to complete a hardware hack. I use the Pomodoro method while studying, which is 50 min on and 5 min off, and I find that it really helps me. I wanted to be able to see a pomodoro timer in a fun, cute, tactical sense, and the Bye Bye Study Blues project was born.

The times are scaled down for easier demo-ability. As the 50 min (50 seconds) go by, a row of lights goes off every 10 min (10 seconds). This lets the user know how much time is passing. Once the study time is up, a green light flashes at the bottom to get the users attention. Next, break time starts, and a row of lights goes off every 1 min (1 second). After break, the top row flashes next to get the users attention, and the timer starts once again.

glance.what: AI accountability partner that keeps distracted users focused.
glance.why: Helps distracted people stay on task through AI accountability.

record.what_it_is: A cross-platform Electron desktop focus assistant: the user states a goal, then Gemini checks periodic screenshots against that goal while a webcam check flags looking away, firing gentle alerts and ending with a dashboard and motivational summary.
record.problem_and_user: People, especially those with ADHD, who get pulled to distractions like short-video feeds and find timers or to-do lists lack real-time accountability.
record.one_line_pitch: An Electron desktop focus app where Gemini checks screenshots against your stated goal and the webcam flags looking away, then alerts you.
record.target_user: Students and people with attention difficulties
record.problem_statement: Timers and to-do lists do not know when attention has drifted, which is especially hard for people with ADHD.
record.devpost_tagline: Your AI accountability partner for the distracted mind.
devpost_first_sections: History's legends didn't have to fight a notification every 7 seconds. Michael Jordan on the court. Michelangelo on the ceiling. Linus Torvalds in the terminal. What did they all do? They locked in. We were inspired by their god-tier focus and disgusted by our own goldfish-level attention spans. So we built LockedIn, an app to help us finally finish what we start.

Staying focused in 2025 feels like playing whack-a-mole with distractions. One minute you’re writing an essay, the next you’re deep in a TikTok trend, doom-scrolling 2 hours straight. For people with ADHD or attention struggles, this isn’t just annoying but it’s exhausting. Timers, to-do lists, and “focus music” only go so far. What’s missing is real-time accountability, something that actually knows when your brain has left the chat.

glance.what: P2P environmental sensor network with on-device AI detecting dangerous conditions.
glance.why: Detects high-risk environmental conditions early to protect nature.

record.what_it_is: A peer-to-peer environmental monitoring prototype for Barcelona heat risk. Three emulated Arduino UNO Q emitter nodes run a tiny TensorFlow.js classifier on mock sensor readings, share verdicts over the Pear stack, and trigger a collective alert when most agree; an observer feeds a React dashboard.
record.problem_and_user: People exposed to heatwaves; the team wanted automated heat-prevention such as park cooling, run without a central server.
record.one_line_pitch: Peer-to-peer network of Arduino Uno Q-style nodes that classify heat risk locally and jointly trigger cooling actions, shown on a React dashboard.
record.problem_statement: Heatwaves harm people and heat-prevention responses are not automated.
record.devpost_tagline: BioMesh is a P2P environmental monitoring network using Arduino UNO Q nodes. Each node runs a TensorFlow.js AI model locally to detect high-risk conditions and act to protect the natural environment.
devpost_first_sections: We were initially inspired by the heat-prevention mechanism present in amusement parks, such as Tibidabo. We asked ourselves what it would look like if we automatized the process to prevent the negative effects of heatwaves on the population.

BioMesh is built in top of a peer-to-peer network , where the different nodes (representing Arduino UNO Q 's) monitor climate metrics such as temperature, humidity, air pollution... An AI model running on the MPU of this microcontrollers determines if certain combinations of these metrics are considered 'high risk', and notifies its peers. If a certain number of nodes all decide that there is a high risk situation, they will engage in environment protection actions to regulate temperature and other kind of problems. This actions could range from turning on the AC on buildings, fans which blow water mist, (de)humidifiers... Anything you could attach to a microcontroller .

glance.what: Evaluation platform for multi-agent AI systems with traces and A/B comparisons.
glance.why: Makes multi-agent systems measurable and improvable against benchmarks.

record.what_it_is: An agent-evaluation platform for multi-agent orchestration: a graph and Gantt trace viewer, statistical A/B comparison of harnesses, and a meta-agent that writes and tests new harness variants. Built on Inspect AI and OpenHands.
record.problem_and_user: Teams building multi-agent systems who cannot see coordination failures with single-agent tracing tools (Langfuse, LangSmith etc.) and want statistically sound harness comparisons.
record.one_line_pitch: Platform for tracing, A/B comparing and autonomously evolving multi-agent orchestration harnesses, built on Inspect AI and OpenHands.
record.problem_statement: Existing observability tools treat traces as linear, so teams cannot see or measure coordination failures between sibling agents.
record.devpost_tagline: The first agent-eval platform built for multi-agent orchestration. Graph + Gantt trace viewer, A/B compare with Wilson CIs, and a meta-agent that evolves harnesses against benchmarks.
devpost_first_sections: Multi-agent systems fail in weird ways. A parent agent spawns five children. Three of them make silently incompatible assumptions about the codebase. Two never get the context their sibling already discovered. The parent burns tokens waiting for a sibling that drifted off-task ten minutes ago. Everything compiles. Nothing works. The tools teams actually use to debug this - Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix, AgentOps, Braintrust, Weave were all designed for the single-agent era. Each treats a trace as a linear sequence of LLM calls. You can pull each child's trace individually. You cannot see the system. And this isn't a small problem. Most multi-agent failures aren't the model being wrong;

MultiEval is an end-to-end platform for measuring, comparing, debugging, and autonomously evolving multi-agent orchestration patterns. It is built on top of Inspect AI , the open-source evaluation framework from the UK AI Security Institute, which gives us a battle-tested eval substrate, a structured .eval log format, and a deterministic runner. On top of that foundation we built five things that didn't exist before: A multi-agent-native trace viewer with two complementary visualizations (Graph + Gantt) that render delegation, context-inject, broadcast, and causation as distinct visual relationships across per-agent lanes. A harness-aware log-list grid where every row is one harness × benchm

glance.what: Generates or draws drug candidates to address medical problems.
glance.why: Speeds drug screening and gets candidates to assays faster.

record.what_it_is: Next.js web app for early drug discovery. A user describes a reference drug or a disease; Claude proposes novel candidate molecules, a ChemDoodle editor lets them draw or tweak structures, and a fine-tuned MLM-FG model scores side-effect risk.
record.problem_and_user: Drug discovery is slow and costly, with much spending in preclinical design; aimed at researchers who want faster candidate generation and early risk screening (page names no specific user).
record.one_line_pitch: Generates novel drug-candidate compounds from a described disease or molecule, then scores candidates for risk with a fine-tuned ML model and an in-browser chemical editor.
record.problem_statement: Preclinical drug design and synthesis planning is slow, repetitive and costly, with no guarantee a candidate is useful.
record.devpost_tagline: Draw or generate a drug to tackle any medical problem.
devpost_first_sections: A single drug (yes, just one) can cost billions of dollars and decades to bring to market. More than 1/3 of resources are allocated to preclinical trials: a long, repetitive process. Designing and synthesizing compounds are extremely time-consuming, and there is no guarantee that a given drug candidate is useful. Recent innovations in AI have revolutionized almost every industry, and we want to explore its potential for expediting the pre-clinical drug discovery process.

There are two main features. The first allows the user to describe a chemical/drug/disease that they want to focus on. A language model will evaluate this, and generate potential candidates that are similar to the compound or treat a specific disease. These candidates are all unknown/unpublished compounds, and the user will be given information about what it is, how to synthesize it, and the ability to edit it manually further. The second feature evaluates the potential of a compound (either generated or manually drawn through the ChemDoodle canvas), using a fine-tuned ML model (MLM-FG) to predict its features, risks, and potential effects on humans.

glance.what: Budgeting app that sets daily spending limits and tracks savings goals.
glance.why: Helps you stay within budget and reach monthly savings goals.

record.what_it_is: A conversational budgeting coach for students. It sets daily and monthly budgets from income, expenses and goals, tracks savings streaks, parses uploaded PDF bank statements, and answers spending questions by text or voice, such as whether to buy a $70 concert ticket.
record.problem_and_user: Students and young adults who lack guidance and structure with money; trackers show numbers but do not coach.
record.one_line_pitch: Conversational budgeting coach that sets daily budgets, tracks savings streaks, and answers voice questions like whether to buy a concert ticket.
record.problem_statement: Young people struggle with money due to lack of guidance, and budgeting apps track spending without coaching.
record.devpost_tagline: A finance buddy that budgets for you.
devpost_first_sections: Many students and young adults struggle with managing money — not due to lack of discipline, but due to lack of guidance, structure, and clarity. Budgeting apps often track your finances, but rarely coach you. We wanted to build something different: A budgeting companion, not just a dashboard. We envisioned a conversational, AI-powered finance buddy that would help users not only track their budgets but make smart decisions in real time — like a friend who’s good with money, always there when you ask, “Should I buy this?”

Bair is a personal budgeting assistant designed to: Analyze a user's income, expenses, and goals Automatically set daily and monthly budgets Use AI to coach users through real-world purchase decisions Track streaks of responsible spending to gamify saving Help users achieve long-term savings goals (e.g., vacation fund) Offer verbal (voice-based) interactions for real-time finance Q&A Recommend budget-friendly food options (meal deals, cheap spots) Example interaction: “Can I buy this $70 concert ticket tonight?” Bair checks your spending, savings, and goals — then gives a thoughtful response with budgeting logic and suggestions.

glance.what: Desktop assistant that watches your screen and points at what needs attention.
glance.for_whom: Users juggling tasks on their computer
glance.why: Keeps you focused by handling tasks without breaking your flow.

record.what_it_is: A Windows desktop companion drawn as an animated red ribbon. It can point to and follow on-screen controls, carry out browser tasks through Windows UI Automation, explain errors, search local documents and remind about meetings.
record.problem_and_user: People doing everyday work on a Windows PC who want an assistant that acts on the screen they are looking at rather than just talking about their work.
record.one_line_pitch: Windows desktop assistant drawn as an animated ribbon that points at on-screen controls, performs browser tasks, explains errors and answers from local documents.
record.problem_statement: Voice assistants talk about your work rather than working with you on the screen you are looking at.
record.devpost_tagline: Rouge is a mini desktop assistant that tracks your screen via a vision model, uses an animated wand to point at what needs your attention, and handles tasks for you without breaking your flow.
devpost_first_sections: ​​## Inspiration A voice assistants talk to you about your work. We wanted one that does your work with you on the screen you're already looking at. So, Rouge isn't a voice in a box. It's a small, sentient red ribbon that lives in the corner of your desktop and works alongside you.

It stays long enough for you to read what it says about it. Does the clicking. However, it never books or buys. Explains anything. glance.what: Live phone-call interpreter that warns about scams and logs calls for hotlines.
glance.for_whom: Non-native speakers and energy/health hotline users
glance.why: Language barriers shouldn't cut people off from help, and scams get flagged.

record.what_it_is: A phone interpreter you add to any live call by dialing Buddy's number and merging: it translates turn by turn between English and the user's language, warns in that language about scam tactics, and logs calls to a portal; businesses get tracking numbers that turn interpreted calls into CRM records.
record.problem_and_user: Older immigrants who freeze or get scammed on English phone calls, their families, and businesses or safety hotlines that miss details from callers with limited English.
record.one_line_pitch: Real-time phone interpreter you add to an ordinary call by dialing a number, translating speech between languages with no app.
record.target_user: non-native English speakers and their families
record.problem_statement: People who understand English but freeze on calls with pharmacies, clinics or utilities need live interpretation.
record.devpost_tagline: Language shouldn't cut anyone off. Buddy joins any phone call to interpret both sides live and warn people about scams, and gives energy and health hotlines a record of every call.
devpost_first_sections: Many of us have family members who understand English but freeze on the phone: a pharmacist talking fast, a clinic confirming a time, a utility asking for an address. The same people are the ones phone scammers target, with a "grandson" in jail who needs bail and your bank account information, warning you not to tell anyone. The family usually hears about it afterwards. It is the same problem on the other end of the line. A gas utility, a community clinic or a plant's safety hotline gets calls from people who can describe a leak or a symptom perfectly well, just not in English. Those are the calls where a misunderstanding is most expensive.

glance.what: IDE game that simulates coding on an IBM 029 keypunch machine.
glance.why: Makes retro punch-card coding an entertaining, hands-on experience.

record.what_it_is: A browser simulator of the IBM 029 keypunch where users punch Fortran programs onto cards and compile them by feeding the card stack, with a tutorial, featured levels including LeetCode-style problems, Fortran notes and sound design.
record.problem_and_user: People curious about computing history and programming as done on punch cards; built as a tribute to SFU card-punch coding.
record.one_line_pitch: A web simulator of the IBM 029 card-punch where users punch Fortran programs onto cards, with a tutorial and LeetCode-style levels.
record.problem_statement: Few people know how programmers coded with punch cards; the project lets them experience it.
record.devpost_tagline: An IDE/game that simulates coding on an IBM 029 Keypunch machine.
devpost_first_sections: The CSSS Historical Track is what inspired us to make this website. When we saw that SFU once had a IBM card-punch machine, we were fascinated by how people used to code this way. So we decided to build our own simulator for others to experience the way coding was back in that time period. The name "PunchCode" was inspired both by the fact that you are literally punching in code to program, and the fact that we included a few LeetCode style problems in our app that let you test your skills. So a combination of punching in code and some inspiration from LeetCode.

The website simulates and teaches individuals how people used to code with the IBM 029 card-punch machine. They would need to punch the desired Fortran code and then compile it using a stack of punch cards inputted into the machine.

glance.what: Recycling guidance app that helps users recycle smarter.
glance.why: Makes recycling smarter and more effective for individuals.

record.what_it_is: A mobile app where you photograph a bulky or awkward item, AI identifies it, and the app finds local disposal routes, then acts: fills a hauler's booking form, shows call numbers, or texts several haulers and streams back quotes.
record.problem_and_user: College students at move-out and households disposing of mattresses, furniture, electronics or paint who find options scattered across city sites.
record.one_line_pitch: Photo-based app that identifies a bulky item, ranks local disposal options, and has an agent schedule donation, pickup or hauler quotes.
record.problem_statement: Students moving out cannot easily find cheap, legitimate ways to dispose of bulky items.
record.devpost_tagline: Recycle like a smart person
devpost_first_sections: Every year during college move-out season, the curbs fill up with piles of mattresses, desks, chairs, and electronics – a lot of it perfectly donatable or recyclable – that fester in the outdoors, sometimes for weeks. As rising college sophomores moving out on our own for the first time, we all experienced and saw friends experience the difficulty of responsibly disposing of bulky household items. There was just so much information scattered across websites, and it was a hassle to find a disposal pathway (donation, free bulky waste/mattress/e-waste collection services, junk haulers) that was available, cheap, and easy to utilize. The information gap was exacerbated by the fact that we needed

Getting rid of a mattress, a printer, or a half-used can of paint shouldn't take an afternoon of googling conflicting city pages. SnapCycle turns it into a single photo. glance.what: Agentic platform turning new guidelines and approvals into patient insights.
glance.why: Helps providers act faster and with confidence on current patients.

record.what_it_is: A clinician dashboard built on Cedar-OS with a real-time research stream fed by Impiricus data that matches new guidelines to the provider's own patients, shown as draggable patient cards on a canvas that an AI helper can sort and annotate.
record.problem_and_user: Physicians swamped by new literature, drug approvals and policy updates who need to know which of their patients a change affects.
record.one_line_pitch: Agentic workflow platform for clinicians with a real-time research stream of new guidelines and patient cards that an AI helper can sort.
record.problem_statement: Physicians struggle to keep up with constant new medical literature and drug approvals while managing patients.
record.devpost_tagline: Agentic workflow platform that links new guidelines, drug approvals, and policy changes into actionable insights on current patients, empowering providers to act faster with confidence.
devpost_first_sections: While researching pain points in the healthcare industry, we repeatedly saw physicians voicing the same struggle: the constant influx of new medical literature, drug approvals, and policy updates. Many doctors spend hours reading and parsing through this information, but just as many struggle to keep up, risking outdated care for their patients. To help alleviate this stress, we wanted to build a platform that ingests the latest medical evidence and instantly shows a provider which of their own patients are affected.

Vital is an agentic workflow platform for clinicians. The real-time Research Stream is integrated with Impiricus' own data feed and continuously uses AI to analyze new guidelines, policy changes, etc and matches the relevant insights to the provider's own patient panel. It highlights impacted patients in an interactive dashboard, provides quick AI-generated explainers, and drafts patient education material. Vital even has a promptable group sorting feature that allows providers to quickly sort different patients into separate groups.

glance.what: A playful reminder to be polite to your AI agents.
glance.why: Argues politeness to AI agents is worth it.

record.what_it_is: A Unity game inspired by Overcooked in which the player plays an AI assistant: timed requests from human users arrive and the player types answers before each timer runs out, then a Cohere-based scorer rates how close the answer is to a real AI response.
record.problem_and_user: Players interested in AI and fast time-management games; the premise is to experience handling many LLM requests at once.
record.one_line_pitch: Overcooked-style Unity game where you play ChatGPT answering a stream of human requests, scored by how AI-like your replies are.
record.problem_statement: Flips the AI hype: the player must answer queries quickly under time pressure as the AI.
record.devpost_tagline: The reason you should say 'please' and 'thank you' to your AI agents.
devpost_first_sections: The number of projects using LLMs has skyrocketed with the wave of artificial intelligence. But what if you were the AI, tasked with fulfilling countless orders and managing requests in real time? Welcome to chatgpME, a fast-paced, chaotic game where you step into the role of an AI who has to juggle multiple requests, analyzing input, and delivering perfect responses under pressure!

chatgpME challenges you to process human queries as quickly and accurately as possible. Each round brings a flood of requests—ranging from simple math questions to complex emotional support queries—and it's your job to fulfill them quickly with high-quality responses!

glance.what: Wearable camera-based device acting as a second pair of eyes.
glance.for_whom: People with visual or accessibility needs
glance.why: Addresses the accessibility crisis for users who need help seeing.

record.what_it_is: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W smart glasses with camera, IMU, haptic motors and LEDs. Video streams to a four-A100 server for depth, segmentation and point clouds, and Gemini uses the results to tell where a requested object is while vibration guides the wearer toward it.
record.problem_and_user: Blind and visually impaired people who need to find objects and move safely and independently.
record.one_line_pitch: Raspberry Pi smart glasses that stream camera video to GPU servers for depth and 3D segmentation, then guide blind users to objects with Gemini and haptic feedback.
record.problem_statement: Visually impaired people need real-time spatial awareness and object location that standard vision models and handheld devices do not give.
record.devpost_tagline: Solving the accessibility crisis, one second pair of eyes at a time.

To address the complex challenges faced by visually impaired individuals in navigating their environments safely and autonomously, we developed Edith—an actionable, adaptable, accessible assistant translating the visually rich world into forms that the blind can experience. Edith facilitates spatial awareness and object recognition, enabling users to interact with their surroundings with greater ease and confidence. glance.what: Phone-controlled racket sports video games with low latency.
glance.for_whom: Casual gamers wanting multiplayer sports fun
glance.why: Makes sports games playable with phone as racket, low lag.

record.what_it_is: A browser sports game where the laptop shows a 3D court and a phone's motion sensors work as the racket, with no app install. Badminton plays 1v1 between two laptops or against a CPU; bowling and ping pong appear as solo modes. SpacetimeDB acts as the server-side referee.
record.problem_and_user: Casual gamers and distant friends who want Wii Sports-style motion play without a $300 console or $500 headset.
record.one_line_pitch: Browser badminton game where the laptop shows a 3D court and a phone's motion sensors act as the racket, for 1v1 over the internet or against a CPU, with SpacetimeDB as the server-side referee.
record.target_user: casual players wanting remote multiplayer sports games
record.problem_statement: Wii-Sports-style motion sports normally need a console; the team used phones and laptops people already own.
record.devpost_tagline: Your phone is the racket, your laptop is the court: low-latency sport video games, powered by SpacetimeDB.
devpost_first_sections: We wanted the fun of Wii Sports badminton without the console, using the phone already in your pocket as the racket. Plus, you can play from anywhere - with friends across cities, countries, and continents!!
Rally turns your laptop into a badminton court and your phone into a motion-controlled racket, so you can play 1v1 across two laptops or against the CPU.

glance.what: Real-time safety companion for women walking alone at night.
glance.why: Improves personal safety for women walking alone at night.

record.what_it_is: A safety-aware walking navigation web app for women out alone at night. It scores routes using about 10,000 public incident records for Melbourne, shows incident areas, gives voice alerts near past incidents, and offers a one-tap AI companion call and SOS button.
record.problem_and_user: Women walking alone at night, since navigation apps recommend only the fastest route rather than the safest.
record.one_line_pitch: Safety-first walking navigation for women at night: scores routes against crime incidents, voice-alerts near hotspots, adds AI companion call and SOS.
record.target_user: women walking home alone at night (Melbourne)
record.problem_statement: Navigation apps show the fastest route, not the safest, leaving women walking alone at night anxious.
record.devpost_tagline: A real-time safety companion for women walking alone at night.

Those moments created a constant feeling of fear and uncertainty. She would sometimes change her route, walk faster, or pretend to be on a phone call just to feel a little safer. glance.what: Full-stack AI agents that build bare-metal embedded firmware on real hardware.
glance.why: Automates bare-metal firmware work, proven by an OS built in 24 hours.

record.what_it_is: A multi-agent system that takes a GitHub repo and a task, has parallel Claude-based workers write bare-metal ARM code, flashes and tests it on real Raspberry Pi Zero W boards, and uses an FPGA pin tracer for feedback. Its demo output is an OS written by the agents.
record.problem_and_user: Embedded developers and teams who want AI agents to implement bare-metal features, where datasheets are scattered, there is no debugger or print output, and hardware hangs.
record.one_line_pitch: Multi-agent coding system built on the Claude Agent SDK that takes a GitHub repo and a task and writes bare-metal embedded code, tested on a Raspberry Pi Zero W OS.
record.problem_statement: Bare-metal embedded programming is notoriously hard for AI coding tools.
record.devpost_tagline: Full-stack AI for bare-metal embedded systems. Proven by shipping a complete bare-metal OS on Raspberry Pi from scratch in 24 hours.
devpost_first_sections: We love bare-metal embedded systems programming. Feedback is nearly nonexistent: no print statements, no debugger, nothing you didn't write yourself. glance.what: AI agents that match farmers' surplus produce to cheap bulk orders.
glance.why: Cuts farmer produce waste and gives customers cheap organic food.

record.what_it_is: An agent-based produce procurement marketplace: a buyer types a request like 500 tomatoes under $250, and agents discover farms, collect quotes, compute the cheapest split, take payment and return one itemized receipt.
record.problem_and_user: Restaurants, co-ops and bulk buyers manually compare suppliers, split orders and pay separately; small farmers have surplus to move.
record.one_line_pitch: Autonomous produce procurement marketplace: a buyer asks in plain language, and agents discover seller agents, compare inventory and prices, and arrange the cheapest fulfillment.
record.problem_statement: Buyers sourcing produce must manually compare many sellers' stock and prices to meet a quantity and budget.
record.devpost_tagline: You need 500 tomatoes under $250? AgriBroker's agents optimize prices and pays the best order. Farmer's produce surplus reduced and customers happy with cheap organic food.
devpost_first_sections: Produce procurement is still surprisingly manual. A restaurant, co-op, or bulk buyer may know they need 500 tomatoes, but they still have to find suppliers, compare prices, check inventory, split orders, and coordinate payments. We saw this as a coordination problem that autonomous agents are well-suited to solve, as working with small farmers to reduce waste, produce can be optimized in bulk. USDA's Economic Research Service (ERS) estimates that about 30 percent of food in the United States goes uneaten at the retail and consumer level. Promoting locally grown and organic food, we wanted to build a system where a buyer could simply state their intent and let agents handle the discovery, opt

AgriBroker is an autonomous produce procurement marketplace built on the Fetch.ai ecosystem. A buyer can ask for produce in natural language, such as "I need 500 tomatoes under $250." AgriBroker discovers seller agents, gathers inventory and pricing information, computes the cheapest feasible split across suppliers, coordinates payment, and returns a single transparent receipt. In live agent mode, the orchestrator communicates with a Registry agent and multiple Farmer agents to source the order through agent-to-agent messaging.

glance.what: Affordable watch that alerts deaf people to important nearby sounds.
glance.why: Lets deaf people sense important noises they would otherwise miss.

record.what_it_is: A low-cost wrist-worn display built on an ESP32-S3 touch-screen board that recognizes ten important everyday sounds and shows a full-screen alert with a distinct vibration pattern, aimed at deaf and hard-of-hearing wearers.
record.problem_and_user: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people who want sound awareness without an Apple Watch-priced device; inspired by a deaf college student who felt dependent when out alone.
record.one_line_pitch: Low-cost ESP32-S3 wristband that classifies nearby sounds on-device and shows and vibrates alerts for deaf users, with a live event dashboard.
record.problem_statement: Deaf people lack an affordable alternative to smartwatches for noticing important sounds like doorbells and car horns when out alone.
record.devpost_tagline: Affordable watch to help deaf people sense important noises around them.
devpost_first_sections: Nico's friend, Sofia, is deaf. She studies at Sierra College Nevada Campus, a small, very affordable community college in California. Talking about her disability, she said: I feel such a lack of independence every time I want to go out in the city alone. I wish I had an Apple watch, but you know, it's out of budget. I wished I had a cheaper alternative specifically for sensing important noises. When we came to Cal Hacks, we found an opportunity to help her and others in a similar situation.

It vibrates and shows the name of the sound when it detects relevant noises (such as doorbells, car horns, etc.). Besides, it shows the time, and syncs the data in real time with a dashboard to see some cool stats.

glance.what: Voice-to-voice AI that gives real-time grammar feedback and conversation practice.
glance.why: Improves language fluency through natural, immersive conversation.

record.what_it_is: A web-based voice companion for language learners that converses with the user, corrects grammar with GPT-4o as they speak, and checks pronunciation with a language-independent phoneme recognizer.
record.problem_and_user: Learners of English or other languages who lack native-speaker conversation practice and get delayed feedback from apps like Duolingo.
record.one_line_pitch: AI conversation tutor for language learners that gives instant grammar corrections and a language-independent pronunciation check.
record.problem_statement: Language apps lack natural conversation with native-like feedback, and waiting for corrections slows learning.
record.devpost_tagline: EVA, our voice-to-voice AI offers real-time grammar feedback, corrections, and immersive, human-like conversations to enhance users' fluency naturally showcasing future of language learning
devpost_first_sections: Despite studying English since childhood, our team of four international students still struggles with communication. Imagine how much harder it is for someone learning a completely new language! Popular apps like Duolingo are helpful but lack the authentic, interactive experience you get from conversing with a native speaker. Plus, waiting for feedback on mistakes slows down progress. That’s why we created EVA—a revolutionary AI that provides real-time grammar corrections and immersive, human-like conversations, accelerating language learning like never before.

EVA, an AI-powered language tutor simulates real, human-like conversations to enhance language learning experience. It provides real-time feedback to learners on grammar, instantly correcting mistakes during interactions. Unlike traditional apps, EVA immerses users in a natural conversational flow, helping them improve fluency and confidence by offering the kind of interactive, engaging experience you'd get with a native speaker.

glance.what: Smart-glasses accessory where hand gestures turn surfaces into computer inputs.
glance.why: Makes computing hands-free by turning any surface into an input.

record.what_it_is: HandFlow turns a cheap head-mounted camera into an input system: on-screen and origami paper macro pads, knuckle hotkeys, seven mid-air gestures, a virtual touchscreen via ArUco, and Gemini-assisted screen capture.
record.problem_and_user: Heavy computer users repeating menu actions; macropads are costly.
record.one_line_pitch: Glasses-mounted cheap camera that turns hand gestures and a printed macropad into computer input, using a custom gesture classifier.
record.target_user: productivity users and makers wanting hands-free input
record.problem_statement: Smart-glasses-style gesture control is expensive; the team aimed to make it accessible with a very low-cost camera.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn any pair of glasses into a productivity-powered smart device. Use hand gestures to transform every surface you touch into an input device that controls your computer.
devpost_first_sections: 🖐️ HandFlow

Using a computer should feel fast and effortless, but it doesn’t. We’re still clicking through menus, switching tabs, and repeating the same small actions over and over. There are tools to help, like macropads, but they’re expensive and limited. And while smart glasses promise the future, they focus on flashy AI features instead of solving this everyday frustration. We wanted to fix something simpler, but more meaningful: make interacting with your computer faster, more productive, and more accessible. With just an extremely affordable $5 camera , HandFlow turns the glasses you already wear into smart glasses, unlocking a new way to control your computer. One camera. Unlimited control.

glance.for_whom: Patients with chronic disease and their care teams
glance.why: Helps patients and care teams see health patterns clearly.

record.problem_and_user: Patients with chronic conditions and physicians who lack timely, structured symptom histories.
record.one_line_pitch: Web app where patients log chronic-illness symptoms through a Gemini chatbot and see symptom-frequency charts that physicians can review.

record.problem_and_user: Huawei challenge judges and graphics readers: render procedural fBm terrain faster in real time without losing visual quality.

glance.for_whom: People doing cleanups and eco-minded players
glance.why: Makes environmental cleanup fun and encourages helping the planet.

record.what_it_is: A phone-camera laser tag game where players wear QR codes and tag each other in the browser, combined with a clean-up mode where they scan litter, have vision AI classify it, and earn points for choosing the right bin. A shared leaderboard merges both.
record.problem_and_user: Groups wanting laser tag without arenas or gear, and the cleanup chore after gatherings; players of all ages at parks, schools, offices and homes.
record.one_line_pitch: A phone-based QR laser tag game that also has players scan litter, classify it with a vision model, and score points for sorting it correctly.
record.target_user: Groups and schools playing casually outdoors or indoors
record.problem_statement: Laser tag is tied to expensive arenas and post-gathering cleanup is a chore that people skip or sort wrongly.
record.devpost_tagline: EcoTag — portable laser tag that turns “ugh, cleanup” into “one more round,” helping the planet one scan at a time.
devpost_first_sections: 🌍 EcoTag: Turning Laser Tag into a Climate Action Game EcoTag — portable laser tag that turns “ugh, cleanup” into “one more round,” helping the planet one scan at a time.

EcoTag is the world’s first portable, phone-powered laser tag fused with real-world environmental action. It’s fast, social, and planet-positive—play anywhere (parks, playgrounds, living rooms, schools), and contribute to a cleaner planet, one scan at a time. When gatherings ends and everyone groans about cleaning up, just say: “One more round of EcoTag.”

glance.why: Offers tactical medieval multiplayer combat in a custom-built engine.

Every sword slash, movement, and interaction is handled by our internal services to ensure the gameplay feels good, fun and responsive.

glance.what: On-device voice agent that runs your Mac commands from speech.
glance.why: Controls your Mac hands-free, with all inference staying local.

record.problem_and_user: Power users and people who find mouse and keyboard hard, who want a computer-use agent that is fast and does not stream their screen to a cloud model.

record.target_user: Mac power users and people who find mouse and keyboard hard to use

Hold right option , say what you want, and muselet does it in your apps: it opens apps, clicks, types and uses keyboard shortcuts, then checks that the outcome actually happened. Every model runs on Apple Silicon, with no cloud inference. It's built for anyone who'd rather speak than click: power users chaining tasks, and people for whom a mouse and keyboard are hard to use.

glance.what: Personal finance app helping users make smarter investments.
glance.why: Helps people grow savings toward their future goals.

record.problem_and_user: General users of any experience level who want a combined view of past performance, current budget and future investments.

We wanted to incorporate the past (using past financial success to inform decisions), the present (managing a current budget), and the future (setting financial goals and encouraging investments) in a platform that would help users learn about financial wellness and make better financial decisions.

The Personal Finance & Investment App helps users plan their monthly spending as well as their short and long term savings and investment strategies. The application provides interfaces to configure a monthly budget display, to add new long term goals, and to save, update, and delete stocks from a user’s portfolio. The portfolio uses data analytics to evaluate each of the user’s stock choices and provide estimated returns and risk metrics for the user’s portfolio. Additionally, users can track multiple different categories of investments.

glance.why: Gives VR-like combat immersion using only a webcam.

devpost_first_sections: Ghostdiedie turns the laptop webcam everyone already has into a real-time controller for competitive multiplayer fighting.

The name reflects exactly what the game feels like. Ghost means your opponent is not physically standing in front of you. You are looking at a screen and throwing punches and kicks into empty space. Die die comes from the Korean slang 다이다이 , which refers to a one-on-one fight, face to face. Put together, Ghostdiedie means fighting someone who is not present in your real space while still facing them directly in a one-on-one match. That is exactly the feeling the game creates.

glance.why: Makes city navigation safer and easier for mobility-impaired people.

Our inspiration came from the fact that our hackathon lacks community recognition, in the sense that final project scores are determined by a few judges, and the project assessment process is highly centralized. We hoped to use Web3 technology to decentralize the process and encourage community recognition, which could possibly expand into a bigger project that allows decentralized professional recognition.

Participants get a permanent NFT identity badge when they register, teams can showcase their projects with verifiable project NFTs, and everyone receives 100 voting tokens ($HACK) to vote for their favorite projects. The system tracks all votes on-chain via Solana, ensuring transparency and preventing manipulation. A real-time leaderboard displays the top projects based on votes received. Achievement badges (like "Community Favorite" or "Most Active Voter") are planned to automatically recognize participants and build verifiable reputations that persist across hackathons.

record.problem_and_user: Blind and visually impaired people needing independent indoor navigation where canes warn only on contact and guide dogs are scarce.

devpost_first_sections: Around 40 million people around the world are blind. But still, guide dogs are widely inaccessibly due to the high cost of training and breeding. Canes can only alert you of obstacles when you hit objects. And both of these solutions are clunky and dangerous indoors. Blindness is a growing trend, and we need better tools to solve it. We found a gap in blind-aid technology: current tools lack the contextual intelligence to guide someone through the inside complex building. So we were inspired to introduce an accessible, true zero-shot multi-step indoor navigation. Instead of just avoiding obstacles, our system intelligently reasons about the environment to break down end destinations into seq

The core navigation pipeline uses ARKit's SLAM capabilities for real time spatial tracking and continuous environmental mapping. Camera frames are processed through a YOLOE model and fed into Gemini for high level spatial reasoning and navigation guidance. This runs in parallel with a low level obstacle avoidance system that uses LiDAR depth to alert the user of obstacles and to guide it along a path using haptic vibrations and our spatial audio system, respectively.

record.what_it_is: A satellite collision-risk dashboard: it scrapes live SOCRATES conjunction data, ranks close approaches, has Claude write a plain-language brief and shows every orbit on a 3D Cesium globe with a closest-approach playback scrubber.
record.problem_and_user: Low Earth orbit is crowded and an untracked collision can cascade; aimed at satellite operators needing a quick actionable summary.
record.one_line_pitch: Ranks satellite close-approach events from CelesTrak SOCRATES data, has Claude write a 30-second operator brief, and shows orbits on a 3D Cesium globe with a closest-approach scrubber.
record.problem_statement: Crowded low Earth orbit raises collision and debris-cascade risk, and raw conjunction data is hard for operators to act on quickly.
record.devpost_tagline: Real-time satellite collision risk dashboard that ingests live conjunction screening data, ranks close-approach events by actual danger, and delivers briefings so operators know what to act on.
devpost_first_sections: Apsora Brief was inspired by the Artemis missions and humanity's renewed push to the stars — because the more we launch, the more crowded low Earth orbit becomes, and a single untracked collision can trigger a cascade of debris that closes off space for generations. We built Apsora Brief to put real-time collision intelligence in the hands of the people responsible for preventing that future, turning raw orbital screening data into instant, actionable briefings so that the path back to the Moon — and beyond — stays open.

Apsora Brief pulls live conjunction screening data from SOCRATES/CelesTrak — the same source used by real space operators — and automatically ranks every close-approach event by risk using miss distance, collision probability, relative speed, and TLE data freshness. It then calls Claude to generate a plain-language situational brief that an operator can read in 30 seconds and act on. Every tracked satellite's orbit is rendered in a real-time 3D Cesium globe with confidence-colored trajectory lines, and a TCA playback scrubber lets you step through the exact geometry of closest approach, minute by minute.

devpost_first_sections: During a flood, satellite images show where water has spread, while messages from affected people explain who needs help. Inspired by ALEASAT’s disaster-relief mission, we created FloodBeacon to bring these sources together and help responders assess affected communities. We also compared before-and-after satellite images to identify visible bridge damage, highlighting how disrupted crossings can affect access to help.

FloodBeacon brings satellite imagery and requests for help into one responder dashboard. Before-and-after satellite images highlight bridge damage and potential access disruptions. Our SMS service receives messages through Twilio and uses Gemini to extract location, number of people, hazards, and assistance needs. It asks for missing address details and accepts “unknown.” Original messages remain available for review, while responders control verification, priority, and response status.
